articles.title: In 2024, Glenn and Barbara Britt left Dartmouth at least $150 million; the gift nearly doubled its zero-parent-contribution income threshold from $65,000 to $125,000 and expanded Tuck scholarships
articles.summary: In March 2024, Dartmouth College in the United States announced that it would receive more than $150 million from the estates of former Time Warner Cable
articles.body: In March 2024, Dartmouth College in the United States announced that it would receive more than $150 million from the estates of former Time Warner Cable CEO Glenn Britt and his wife, Barbara Britt. The donation, the largest bequest dedicated entirely to scholarships in Dartmouth's 255-year history, was intended to make education more affordable for students from middle-income families. It also provided additional scholarship funding for students at Dartmouth's Tuck School of Business.According to the college, the gift allowed Dartmouth to nearly double the annual family income threshold under which parents are not expected to contribute towards their children's undergraduate education. The limit increased from $65,000 to $125,000 for families with typical assets. Dartmouth said the revised threshold was the most generous of its kind in the United States at the time.Under the arrangement, three-quarters of the donation was allocated to undergraduate financial aid, while the remaining quarter was set aside for scholarships at Tuck. The new policy was scheduled to take effect in the 2024–25 academic year, covering eligible students already enrolled at Dartmouth as well as incoming members of the Class of 2028.The announcement came years after Glenn Britt's death in 2014. Barbara Britt died in August 2023. Dartmouth said the exact value of their bequest would be determined once their estate was fully settled, although the college and Tuck were assured of receiving at least $150 million.Donation changed financial aid at DartmouthBefore the Britts' donation, Dartmouth did not require a parental contribution from families earning $65,000 or less annually, provided they had typical assets. The bequest raised that income threshold to $125,000, extending the benefit to more middle-income households.According to Dartmouth, the change was expected to provide financial relief to approximately 350 families each year across its four undergraduate classes.However, zero parent contribution does not mean students have no financial responsibility. Under the policy, eligible students are still expected to contribute money earned through summer jobs and employment on campus. Dartmouth said this student contribution would not exceed $5,000 annually.The change built on Dartmouth's existing financial aid policies. The college had already introduced need-blind undergraduate admissions for applicants regardless of citizenship, committed to meeting 100% of demonstrated financial need and replaced required undergraduate loans with expanded scholarships.Speaking about the donation, Dartmouth President Sian Leah Beilock said, “Glenn Britt credited Dartmouth for transforming his life, and he was tremendously grateful for the financial aid award that made his Dartmouth experience possible.”She added, “This remarkable bequest from Glenn and Barbara ensures that, regardless of background, the dream of a Dartmouth education can become a reality.”Tuck School of BusinessThe donation also marked an important development for Dartmouth's Tuck School of Business, where Glenn Britt completed his MBA in 1972.Dartmouth described the portion allocated to Tuck as the largest single outright gift in the business school's history. The funding was intended to establish long-term scholarship support through the Britt Scholars programme.The scholarships were designed to help Tuck attract talented students, including those facing greater financial difficulties. Dartmouth specifically highlighted first-generation students, who accounted for 19% of Tuck's Class of 2025.Matthew Slaughter, then dean of Tuck, said the scholarships would continue supporting deserving students in the couple's names.“Having a cohort of Britt Scholars in perpetuity will ensure we continue to provide a life-altering Tuck education to the most deserving students, in Glenn’s and Barbara’s names,” he said.Who were Glenn and Barbara Britt?Glenn Britt grew up in Nyack, New York, in a family of modest financial means. He attended Dartmouth with the help of a substantial financial aid award and graduated in 1971 with a degree in economics.During college, he participated in the marching band and worked at the student radio station, WDCR. He later earned his MBA from Tuck and joined Time Inc., beginning a career in telecommunications.Britt became president of Time Warner Cable in 1999 and CEO in 2001. During his tenure, the business grew from a $6 billion division into an independent publicly traded company generating $21 billion in annual revenue.Barbara Britt, meanwhile, studied history at Douglass College, then the women's college at Rutgers University. She worked as a journalist and photographer for Time's in-house publication, FYI. The couple married in 1975.Both supported educational and cultural organisations, including the Manhattan Theatre Club. Barbara also remained involved in conservation, animal welfare and educational outreach.Glenn Britt maintained a relationship with Dartmouth long after graduating. He supported the college financially, volunteered as an admissions ambassador and served on the Tuck Board of Advisors.The couple also supported technology education through Tuck's Glassmeyer/McNamee Center for Digital Strategies. Their Britt Impact Technology Series introduced students to developments in technology and related career opportunities.Get the latest Education News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Cuánto dinero cobra un legionario, un militar y un sargento del Ejército de España
articles.standfirst: Este lunes, 12 de octubre, se celebra el Día de la Hispanidad
articles.summary: Este lunes, 12 de octubre, se celebra el Día de la Hispanidad
articles.body: Como cada año, este lunes, 12 de octubre, se celebra el Día de la Hispanidad (también conocido popularmente como Día de la Fiesta Nacional), una fecha que conmemora el arribo de Cristóbal Colón a América en 1492. Además, en el ámbito católico, coincide con la festividad de la Virgen del Pilar, patrona de la Hispanidad y de la Guardia Civil. En este sentido y en relación al habitual desfile, os contamos cuánto dinero cobra un legionario, un militar y un sargento del Ejército de nuestro país. Aproximadamente, un legionario gana en torno a 1.200 y 1.400 euros netos al mes, un sargento percibe entre 1.500 y 1.800 euros netos, y para el resto de militares el sueldo varía desde los 1.000 euros netos de un soldado base hasta más de 3.300 euros netos en los rangos más altos. Los legionarios no cuentan con un salario especial por su unidad, sino que se rigen por la misma escala retributiva que el resto de los miembros de las Fuerzas Armadas Españolas, dentro del grupo de Tropa y Marinería. Por su parte, los salarios del personal del Ejército de Tierra se componen de un sueldo base según su subgrupo de funcionario y diversos complementos (empleo, específico, antigüedad por trienios y dedicación especial). articles.title: NLSIU Bengaluru announces NLSAT 2027 for BA, LLB, MPP and PhD admissions; applications to open in November
articles.summary: The National Law School of India University (NLSIU), Bengaluru, has announced its admission schedule for the academic year 2027-28 through the National
articles.body: The National Law School of India University (NLSIU), Bengaluru, has announced its admission schedule for the academic year 2027-28 through the National Law School Admission Test (NLSAT) 2027. According to the notification issued on October 9, the entrance examination will be conducted on April 25, 2027, at designated test centres across India.The university will offer admissions to its Bachelor of Arts (Honours), three-year Bachelor of Laws (LLB Honours), Master’s Programme in Public Policy (MPP) and PhD programmes through the admission process. Application forms for these programmes are scheduled to be released on the university’s official website, nls.ac.in, in November 2026.The academic session for the admitted candidates is scheduled to commence on July 1, 2027.NLSAT 2027 examination date and application scheduleAs per the admission notification, NLSAT 2027 will be held on Sunday, April 25, 2027. Candidates seeking admission to the listed programmes will have to appear for the entrance examination as prescribed by the university.The application process is expected to begin in November 2026. Candidates should regularly check the official NLSIU website for the application link, programme-specific eligibility criteria, submission deadlines, examination details and other admission instructions.The university has advised prospective applicants to refer to the relevant admission notifications before applying to ensure that they meet the requirements for their chosen programme.Which programmes will be offered through NLSAT 2027?NLSIU will conduct admissions through NLSAT 2027 for undergraduate, postgraduate and doctoral programmes. The courses cater to students interested in humanities, legal education, public policy and academic research.BA (Honours)The university offers a three-year undergraduate BA (Honours) programme, with an option to pursue an additional fourth year focused on research.The course structure includes foundational courses, majors, minors, electives, language courses, practical learning and internships. The programme is designed to provide students with a broad academic foundation while allowing them to explore specific areas of interest.Three-year LLB (Honours)The three-year postgraduate LLB (Honours) programme is open to graduates from different academic backgrounds who wish to pursue legal education and build careers in the legal profession.Unlike five-year integrated law courses that students can join after Class 12, this programme is intended for candidates who have already completed an undergraduate degree. Applicants should check the university’s detailed notification for the prescribed eligibility conditions.Master’s Programme in Public PolicyNLSIU will also offer admission to its two-year Master’s Programme in Public Policy. The programme focuses on public policy, social sciences and law.It is intended for candidates interested in understanding policy development, governance and the role of legal and social institutions in public affairs.PhD programmesThe university will conduct admissions to doctoral programmes in Law and in Social Sciences, Humanities and Public Policy.Candidates interested in pursuing research should consult the respective PhD admission notification for details of eligibility, the application process and other selection requirements.How to check the NLSIU admission notificationCandidates can follow these steps to access the admission notification for the academic year 2027-28:Visit the official website, nls.ac.in.Navigate to the admissions section of the website.Look for the NLSAT 2027 admission notification for the relevant programme.Open the notification and read the eligibility criteria, examination details and application instructions.Check the website again in November 2026 for the release of application forms and further admission-related announcements.Candidates should rely on the official university website for updates regarding the application process, examination schedule and programme-specific requirements.Get the latest Education News and Live updates.
